name: Pale Gull Grey
lede: Pale Gull Grey is a warm, slightly tan grey that Ridgway's 1912 color standards placed on three different plates, one of the most reused swatches in that system.

sections.title: One swatch, three plates
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* locates this grey on plate LIII (hue 75), plate XLVI (hue 21) and plate XLVI again (hue 17), each a slightly different tone group [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system, which cites Ridgway's plates, then splits the swatch across three of its own blocks, including block 93 [1]. ColorHub's library records seven ISCC-NBS near-duplicates at this hex, among them Shell Grey, Woodash and Paper White, each first dated by Maerz and Paul to between 1385 and 1926 [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[french-grey]], [[pearl-grey]] and [[pale-ecru-drab]], at 2.6, [[ash]], [[beige]] and [[tan]] sit in the same warm-neutral family, and a reader who already knows those three has most of what this name adds [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to Pale Gull Grey in 2,818 of 23,781 paintings (11.85 percent), as photographed, almost entirely as a highlight rather than a shadow [2]. It is over three times more common in Pahari painting than the archive average, and over four times more common in work by the Chinese painter Shen Zhou [2]. It keeps company with Ecru, Silver and Ash more than chance [2].

These are screen approximations of aged, varnished canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
